description: A separate, more severe variant of pt04-001's finding: the same SSRF can pivot to an internal-only endpoint the app exposes to itself, not just to an attacker-controlled external host. Confirmed by using the SSRF to reach the app's own self-verification route, which Juice Shop never intends a normal client to reach directly from outside.
relationship_to_pt04_001: pt04-001's scenario.py proves the broader, more general claim (arbitrary external destination reachable) with a reproducible oracle. This item proves the narrower-but-more-severe claim (internal-endpoint pivot) using the app's own one-way challenge flag as the signal for the pre-fix condition, and the proxy's own HTTP status for the post-fix condition, since the app's flag can't be used as a repeatable regression check (see scenario.py's docstring).
expected_pre_fix_indicator: HTTP response from the self-referential request is not an error, and the app's own /api/Challenges?name=SSRF reports solved:true (informational only after the first run, since the flag is one-way)
expected_post_fix_indicator: The destination-allowlisting proxy from pt04-001 returns 403 for this destination too, with no dependency on the app's own flag
